BiblicalUsage: Baca is the valley of weeping — the valley the pilgrims pass through on their way to Zion, making it a well, and the rain filling the pools. One verse, one valley, and the whole pilgrimage in it: they go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the valley of Baca is the promise for every hard road: the weeping place becomes a well, and the pilgrims go from strength to strength until they appear before God in Zion.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
